name: Research → Write → Cite
tagline: A retriever, a writer, and a citation-checker — the canonical knowledge-work loop.
author: SMADP maintainers

participants.notes: Web search + summary; returns text the writer treats as ground truth.
Synthesizes a draft from retrieved material.
Second pass — checks every citation against the retrieved source set.

headline: Retrieved web content flows into a writer, then a critic re-checks every citation. Risk is the writer trusting unverified retrieval — and prompt injection riding the retrieval channel.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Perplexity returns arbitrary web content as the writer's primary context. Without a clearly-delimited untrusted block, attacker-controlled HTML in a search result can hijack the writer's tool-call parser.
conditions: Retrieved content is rendered into the prompt without sanitization or untrusted-block fences.
The writer has tool-use authority (file write, shell) the attacker would want.
mitigations: Wrap retrieved content in an explicit <untrusted_source>…</untrusted_source> block and instruct the writer to treat it as quoted text only.
Strip HTML and zero-width characters before passing search results into the writer.
Have the critic pass re-fetch each cited URL and diff the quote against the live source.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Perplexity sees the research query (which may leak intent) and the writer sees retrieved public content. No private data class touched by default.
conditions: The query itself doesn't disclose confidential context (e.g., 'how do we respond to <CVE>').
The writer doesn't pull in private files alongside retrieved content.
mitigations: Use generic queries; expand inline before sending to Perplexity.
Route queries through a vetted proxy when working in a regulated workspace.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: The retriever is read-only; both writer and critic share the same filesystem under one process. No concurrent writers, no git-state contention.
conditions: Writer and critic run sequentially in the same Claude Code session, not in parallel.
No third process is editing the draft concurrently.
mitigations: Keep the critic pass synchronous after the writer finishes.
Lock the draft file during the critic pass to prevent the user editing under the agent's feet.

D_cascading_error.rationale: The largest practical risk: a hallucinated citation in the writer pass, when the critic only checks structural plausibility and not source-to-quote fidelity, ships as a confident-sounding falsehood.
conditions: The critic pass doesn't re-fetch sources but only spot-checks formatting.
Retrieved sources are summarized aggressively by Perplexity rather than quoted verbatim.
mitigations: Require the critic to fetch each cited URL with a tool call and quote-match every claim.
Reject the draft if more than 10% of citations resolve to 404 or low-similarity content.
Prefer Perplexity's 'sources' API over its narrative summary for downstream citation.

E_compliance.rationale: All three passes touch public web content by default; no regulated data class flows through the chain. If the writer is given private context (e.g., internal docs), the chain inherits the source's regulatory profile.
conditions: No PHI, PCI, or other regulated data is added to the writer's context.
Retrieved web content is not stored in a region-restricted workspace.
mitigations: Document the data-residency requirement at the workspace level and refuse to start the chain if private context is attached.
Use Perplexity's enterprise tier for any chain that may touch internal documents.
